opus.problem: Nearly the same fact as clue 2. Both say the Jews committed to keep these days every year for all time (bound themselves every year vs. remembered by every generation so the memory never fades).
Nearly the same fact as clue 4. Both say a letter was sent to confirm these days (Esther with Mordecai wrote to confirm a second letter vs. Mordecai sent letters to confirm these days).

The best-known facts about Purim are left out: the feasting and gladness, sending gifts of food to one another and gifts to the poor (Esther 9:19, 22), and the 14th and 15th of Adar, with Susa keeping the 15th (Esther 9:18-21). Instead, five clues come from Esther 9:27-31 and repeat the yearly-observance and letter-confirmation details. Replace the overlapping clues with these better-known stories.
